question: Which exact 3.1.32 entry points back the Supervisor platform services that Band 10 Pro and Band 11 already have (monotonic clock, heap, lseek/mkdir/rmdir/fsync, battery, wake locks, screen state and wake, manual brightness, properties, MiWear link state), and which earlier ensemble records are wrong?
prototype_hypothesis: Same AAPCS contracts as the Band 10 Pro .043 / Band 11 platform hooks (EVID-PLATFORM-HW-1043-001, EVID-PLATFORM-HW-4155-001), called from the UI owner thread; battery uses the ready + snapshot pair like Band 11.
callsite_evidence: NuttX functions carry their source path in DEBUGASSERT: clock/clock_gettime.c -> 0xC13B1D8, vfs/fs_lseek.c -> lseek 0xC3932BC (file_seek 0xC3913EC), vfs/fs_mkdir.c -> 0xC39146C, vfs/fs_rmdir.c -> 0xC391C58, vfs/fs_fsync.c -> 0xC3934E0, mm_heap/mm_malloc.c -> mm_malloc 0xC16A8C0 behind malloc 0xC16AE80, mm_heap/mm_free.c -> mm_free 0xC16A300 behind free 0xC16A424 (both on g_mmheap 0x2007D6EC).
clock_gettime writes {int64 tv_sec, int32 tv_nsec}; MiWearScreen 0xC45FBEC calls it with CLOCK_REALTIME and multiplies tv_sec by 1000000.
lseek keeps the 64-bit offset in r2:r3 and whence on the stack, the same shape as .043.
struct stat here is 96 bytes (nx_stat 0xC391E50 clears 96, st_size at +24), not the 104-byte .043 layout, so stat is not recorded; the Supervisor's opendir + lseek fallback is used.

uv_topic_battery_state_cb 0xC45F0C8 (PowerManager) sets the charging-ready byte 0x2009A880 and the level-ready byte 0x2009A881, the charging flag 0x2009A884 and the level dword 0x2009A888; 0xC45A458 returns ready-and-ready, 0xC45A474 copies the two words to out[0..1].

PowerManager wakelock_create 0xC45DEEC logs 'succeeded, levelAndFlags=%lu, tag=%s' and wraps a 'wakelock' screen session; acquire 0xC4600FC counts and starts the session on the first hold, calling screen_turn_on("wakelock", 26) when flag 0x10000000 is set; release 0xC4601DC.

MiWearScreen __func__ strings map screen_turn_on 0xC45FFF0 and screen_session_{set_auto_brightness 0xC45DD90, restore_default 0xC45DCFC, stop 0xC45DC28}; create 0xC45CD58, start 0xC45DB9C and set_brightness_value 0xC45DE20 are the calls in the stock alarmclock_media_dim_screen sequence create -> start(s, 0) -> set_auto_brightness(s, 2) -> set_brightness_value(s, 60), the order the Supervisor uses.

screen_get_state 0xC45A50C returns 2 while a keep-on hold is counted, otherwise the applied state byte; async_apply_screen_state_change 0xC45FC54 turns the backlight off for 0, on for 2 and treats 1 as AOD.

property_get 0xC3E6B08 returns the value length or -22 for a missing key with a NULL default; property_get_int32 0xC3E6D7C is property_get + strtol(base 0) returning the default on error; 0xC3E6C54 is the int64 variant and 0xC3E6BBC the bool variant.
system_get_state 0xC38B6FC reads system_all_state through the pointer 0x200A8F88 and spins with 'Please call system_init_state first.' while it is NULL; state 1 is byte +1 (get_connect_state).

Ensemble records refuted: clock_gettime 0xC452348 is a UI event handler, heap_malloc 0xC434C1C a C++ copy helper, heap_free 0xC2B8864 is not mm_free, lseek 0xC3BA3F8 an L2CAP state handler, bt_adapter_get_instance 0xC382560 a field store, bt_adapter_get_state 0xC465254 a GATT helper. The Supervisor generated before this review called 0xC452349 as its monotonic clock.
ownership_analysis: Wake-lock objects and brightness sessions are created once per Supervisor slot and kept; wakelock_create stores the tag pointer, so the tag must be static. heap_malloc/heap_free share one heap. Nothing here takes ownership of caller buffers beyond the call.
unsafe_assumptions: The vibrator is preset-only on this build: miwear_vibrator_run 0xC4777FC takes a 12-byte block whose type byte selects one of 31 stock patterns, with no duration; no duration-based entry point is recorded, so haptics stays UNSUPPORTED.
No Bluetooth adapter getter/state entry point was recovered (the stack is Bluelet, not the framework adapter API); adapter state stays unknown.
screen_session_set_auto_brightness status 2 is taken from the stock dim-screen callers, not from the status-name table.
recommended_probe: all-services-test on Mirage (emulator evidence only), then on a device: battery, wake lock, wake screen and brightness override.
